name: Appendages (Category)
summary: The types of Appendages a Droid has determines how well it is able to touch, hold, lift, carry, push, pull, or place objects. A limb that isn't used for Locomotion or balance has one of the following types of Appendages: Probe, Instrument, Tool Mount, Hand, or Claw.

name: Armor (Category)
summary: Protective Armor exists in the Star Wars universe, but only the lightest types see widespread use. Heavier Armor is considered to be too expensive, too restrictive, and just not worth the trouble unless it serves an additional function (such as providing environmental protection, as in the case of Imperial Snowtrooper

fields.armor_bonus_to_reflex_defense: When you are wearing the armor, you add this value as an armor bonus to your Reflex Defense (instead of adding your Heroic Level to your Reflex Defense).
fields.availability: Some armor has limited availability, as indicated below.
fields.cost_credits: The cost of the Armor. Armor sized for Small characters cost half as much, while Armor for Large characters costs double the listed price. Some Armor has limited availability (see Rare, below).
fields.equipment_bonus_to_fortitude_defense: When you are wearing the armor, you add this value as an Equipment bonus to your Fortitude Defense. Some types of Armor do not provide an Equipment bonus to your Fortitude Defense.
fields.heavy_armor: Top of the line Armor, primarily used by military specialists, and high-spec mercenaries.
fields.licensed_restricted_military_or_illegal: Ownership of the armor is limited to certain people, as described in Restricted Items, below.
fields.light_armor: The most common Armors, found anywhere from civilians to experienced hunters.
fields.maximum_dex_bonus: This is the maximum bonus you can apply to your Reflex Defense from Dexterity when wearing this type of Armor. Heavier Armor limits your mobility, reducing your ability to avoid attacks. For example, an Armored Flight Suit has a maximum Dexterity bonus of +3. A character with a Dexterity of 18 normally gains a +4 bonus to their Reflex Defense from Dexterity, but if they're wearing an Armored Flight Suit, they only apply a +3 bonus to their Reflex Defense.
fields.medium_armor: Considered the standard other Armors compare themselves to, these Armors are typically used by military troopers, and various militia.
fields.rare: This armor is generally only available by going to its planet of origin or by acquiring it directly from its wearer (for example, getting Vonduun Crabshell armor from a Yuuzhan Vong warrior). When available on the open market elsewhere, these items usually cost double the listed price, sometimes much more.
fields.speed: Medium Armor and Heavy Armor reduces your Speed to three-quarters normal (rounded down). The individual tables per Armor Proficiency show these reductions if you have a speed of 6 squares or 4 squares. In addition, when wearing Heavy Armor, you can only move up to three times your speed when Running (instead of four times your Speed).
fields.weight_kg: The weight of the Armor. Armor fitted for Small characters weighs half as much. Armor fitted for Large characters weighs twice as much.

name: Bellow (Category)
summary: As a Standard Action, a [Species] can make a special attack roll (1d20 + its Character Level) and compares the result to the Fortitude Defense of all creatures and unattended objects in a 6-Square Cone. A successful hit deals 3d6 points of Sonic damage; if the attack misses, the target takes half damage instead.

name: Double Weapons (Category)
summary: You can attack with both ends of a Double Weapon as a Full-Round Action, but both attack rolls take a -10 penalty (although certain Feats and Talents can reduce these penalties).

name: Droid Talent Trees (Category)
summary: At 1st level and every odd-numbered Heroic Level thereafter (3rd, 5th, 7th, etc.), a character gains a Talent from any one of the Talent Trees available to it. summary: Exotic Weapons are unusual or unique weapons that require specific training to properly utilize (including both Exotic Weapons (Ranged) and Exotic Weapons (Melee)). summary: A Force-user who dies in the process of fulfilling their Destiny may manifest as a Force Spirit. For a Jedi or other good Force-users, this means transforming into a translucent blue spirit that can appear before their former allies. summary: Full-Round Actions consume all of your effort during a given round, effectively replacing all other Actions on your turn. Some uses of Skills require a Full-Round Action to complete. name: Move Actions (Category)
summary: A Move Action represents Actions pertaining to physical movement. The most common Move Action is moving up to your Speed. name: Natural (Category)
summary: Hazards with the Natural Keyword are created with no intervention from sentient beings.

name: Poison (Category)
summary: Poisons are Hazards that are harmful or fatal to creatures. They always attack the Fortitude Defense of a target, ignoring Equipment bonuses to Fortitude Defense, Damage Reduction, and Shield Rating. If a Poison moves a target down the Condition Track, it likely imposes a Persistent Condition as well, which cannot be r

name: Rage (Category)
summary: Once per day, a [Species] can fly into a Rage as a Swift Action. While Raging, the [Species] temporarily gains a +2 Rage bonus on melee attack rolls and melee damage rolls, but cannot use Skills that require patience and concentration, such as Mechanics, Stealth, or Use the Force. A fit of Rage lasts for a number of ro

name: Ranged Weapons (Category)
summary: At any given time, hundreds of manufacturers are creating and marketing a wide array of ranged weapons. These weapons run the gamut from small, concealable handheld weapons to tripod-mounted cannons that require a small crew to operate.

name: Scent (Category)
summary: At close range (within 10 squares), [Species] ignore Concealment and Cover for purposes of Perception checks, and take no penalty from poor visibility while Tracking.

name: Shapeshift (Category)
summary: [Species] are shapechangers and can alter their appearance at will (see the Deception skill). While Shapeshifted, a [Species] gains a +10 Species bonus on Deception checks made to disguise appearance. Additionally, a [Species] can disguise its appearance as a Full-Round Action at no penalty.

name: Simple Weapons (Category)
summary: Simple Weapons include weapons that require no special training to use (including Grenades, Simple Weapons (Ranged), and Simple Weapons (Melee)). Unarmed Attacks and Natural Weapons are considered Light Simple Weapons in which all characters are proficient. Weapon Proficiency (Simple Weapons) is a Starting Feat for all

name: Standard Actions (Category)
summary: Standard Actions are usually the most important Action you'll take in a round, and it often consists of some sort of attack- swinging a Lightsaber, firing a blaster, throwing a punch, hurling a Grenade, and so on. You can perform one Standard Action on your turn.

A Force Talent Tree is any Talent Tree that isn't limited to a particular Heroic Cl

name: Vehicles (Category)
summary: The term "Vehicle" encompasses both Planetary Vehicles (such as Airspeeders, Landspeeders, and Walkers), and Starships (such as Starfighters, Space Transports, and Capital Ships). The major difference between Planetary Vehicles and Starships is that Planetary Vehicles generally do not travel in the vacuum of space. Rul

fields.airspeeders: Airspeeders are repulsorlift Vehicles that can travel anywhere up to about 300 kilometers above ground level, but they are incapable of true space flight. Because they fly so high above the ground, they ignore penalties for Difficult Terrain and obstacles. Of all Planetary Vehicles, Airspeeders are the most maneuverable. Airspeeders can also be used to form Fighter Groups.
fields.attack_rolls: Gunner's Base Attack Bonus + Vehicle's Intelligence modifier + miscellaneous bonuses (Point-Blank Shot, Weapon Focus, etc.) +2 (if Trained in Pilot and firing Vehicle Pilot-controlled Weapon Systems from the Pilot's position).
fields.availability: Whether or not the Vehicle is a Restricted Item.
fields.capital_ships: Capital Ships include all Starships of Colossal (Frigate) size or larger. Capital Ships usually carry hundreds, if not thousands of crewmembers and passengers, and some are large enough to house other Capital Ships within their hangar bays. Some very large transports and colony ships fall into this category, despite not being designed for combat.
fields.cargo_capacity: The amount of cargo the Vehicle can carry.
fields.carried_craft: Other Vehicles that are usually carried aboard this Vehicle.
fields.challenge_level_cl: Heroes gain Experience Points (XP) for disabling, destroying, or otherwise overcoming the Vehicle based on the Vehicle's CL. However, they don't gain additional XP for incidental crew or passengers killed as a result of the Vehicle's destruction.
fields.cover: The amount of Cover the Vehicle grants to its crew and passengers, listed as none, +5 (Normal Cover), +10 (Improved Cover), or Total Cover.
fields.crew: The number and quality of the crew (see Crew Quality). The crew modifiers are already included in all other statistics in the Vehicle description.
fields.damage_threshold: The Vehicle's Damage Threshold is equal to its Fortitude Defense + size modifier.
fields.fighting_space: The Fighting Space that the Vehicle occupies at Character Scale, Starship Scale, or both.
fields.fortitude_defense: The Vehicle's Fortitude Defense is equal to 10 + Strength bonus.
fields.grapple: The Vehicle's Grapple modifier is mainly used to resist attempts to restrain the Vehicle physically (usually via Tractor Beam). A Vehicle's Grapple modifier is equal to its Pilot's Base Attack Bonus + the Vehicle's Strength modifier + the Vehicle's special size modifier;
fields.hyperdrive: The multiplier used when calculating hyperspace travel times (see Astrogation). If the Starship has a backup Hyperdrive, its multiplier is listed in parentheses. Hyperdrive is never used in Character Scale. If the Vehicle has no Hyperdrive, this line is absent.
fields.maximum_velocity: The Maximum Speed the Vehicle can achieve after using All-Out Movement for at least one full round. Maximum Velocity is never used in Starship Scale.
fields.passengers: The number of passengers (including troops) that the Vehicle can carry, in addition to its crew.
fields.payload: The Vehicle's complement of Grenades, Rockets, Missiles, and Torpedoes. If this Vehicle has no Payload, this line is absent.
fields.reflex_defense: The Vehicle's Reflex Defense is equal to 10 + size modifier + Armor bonus (or Pilot's Heroic Level) + Dexterity bonus.
fields.skills: Character's appropriate Skill modifiers (+ Vehicle size modifier + Vehicle Dexterity modifier in the case of the Initiative and Pilot skills).
fields.space_stations: Though not technically modes of transportation, Space Stations have statistics like other Starships. A Space Station can have a population in the thousands or millions, depending on its size. Most Space Stations are immobile, The Death Star being a notable exception.
fields.space_transports: Space Transports are mid-sized Starships of Colossal or Colossal (Frigate) size, with fewer than 200 Hit Points. Most Space Transports are designed for moving passengers or cargo, but some are used as gunships, drop ships, or assault shuttles.
fields.speeders: Speeders are common sights on the technologically advanced worlds. Equipped with repulsorlift drive technology, they hover above the ground at a height of anywhere from a few centimeters, to several meters, and can achieve remarkable speeds. Speeders ignore penalties for Difficult Terrain.
fields.starfighters: Starfighters are small, agile Starships of Gargantuan size or smaller. Though they can travel in atmosphere, they excel at space combat. Starfighters can function with as few as one crewmember (the Vehicle Pilot). Starfighters can also be used to form Fighter Groups.
fields.tracked_vehicles: Tracked Vehicles have treads or tracks looped around a large number of wheels, providing great traction, but making them less maneuverable at higher speeds- and extremely loud at any speed. Tracked Vehicles ignore penalties for Difficult Terrain, and take half damage from Collisions with obstacles at least one size category smaller than them.
fields.vehicle_initiative: The Pilot's Initiative modifier (or the Pilot skill modifier if you are Trained) + Vehicle's size modifier + Vehicle's Dexterity modifier.
fields.walkers: Walkers move about on two or more legs, literally walking over the terrain. Walkers retain their balance by means of finely tuned gyroscopes, and offer a fairly smooth ride. They rely on even footing, however, and when they topple, the results can be disastrous. Walkers ignore obstacles that are three or more sizes smaller than them.
fields.weapon_emplacements: Weapon Emplacements are a staple of ground warfare. They typically fall under two categories: antipersonnel and antivehicle. Weapon Emplacements are treated as Vehicles for statistical purposes, but they are usually immobile and do not require a Vehicle Pilot to function. Instead, Gunners control all the functions of the Weapon Emplacement.
fields.wheeled_vehicles: Wheeled Vehicles move on one or more wheels (most commonly two to four). Faster and more maneuverable than Tracked Vehicles or Walkers, wheels are a cheap alternative to repulsorlift technology for light and fast Vehicles.

fields.damage: The damage the weapon deals with each hit. Melee Weapons also add the wielder's Strength bonus to damage, or twice the wielder's Strength bonus when wielded in two hands.

fields.one_handed: If the weapon's size category is the same as your size (a Human using a Medium weapon such as a Heavy Blaster Pistol), then the weapon is One-Handed.

fields.stun_setting: If the weapon has a Stun Setting, it is listed here. A weapon set to Stun does Stun Damage equal to its normal damage.
fields.too_large: If the weapon's size category is two or more steps larger than your size (an Ewok using a Large weapon, such as a Blaster Cannon), the weapon is Too Large to use. The exceptions to this are Vehicle Weapons, which are housed in a unit that aids in their use.
fields.two_handed: If the weapon's size category is one step larger than your size (a Human using a Large weapon, such as a Light Repeating Blaster), then the weapon requires two hands to use (and sometimes a special mount such as a tripod).
